chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the earnings of the cupper, and he said: “There is no harm in it.”

key_terms.الْحَجَّامِ: the cupper; one who performs cupping or bloodletting
key_terms.كَسْبِ: earnings or income acquired through work
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is unobjectionable or permissible

ai.seo_question: Is the income earned by a cupper permissible in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the permissibility of the earnings of a cupper. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that there is no harm in such income, indicating that this form of livelihood is halal (permissible).
